articleHeadlineTranslated: How Wildlife Trade Triggers the Risk of a New Pandemic
articleHeadline: Bagaimana Perdagangan Satwa Liar Picu Risiko Pandemi Baru
articleSummary: Illegal wildlife trade drives zoonotic risk and could spark new pandemics, according to IPB University ecogenetics expert Ronny Rachman Noor. Globally, outbreaks such as SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 trace to human–wildlife interactions. Mammals traded internationally are 1.5 times more likely to harbor zoonotic pathogens—most commonly coronaviruses, influenza, rabies, and other zoonotic parasites—than non-traded species. Captured wildlife are stressed, lowering immunity and increasing viral shedding; during transport they are crowded with mixed species, elevating cross-species pathogen exchange. Direct contact with blood, meat, or bodily fluids during sale or consumption also creates transmission routes; pets may carry pathogens into homes. Notably, 2022 illegal-trade cases of the king hawk, owa ungko, and golden cat in West Sumatra illustrate this risk. Social media facilitates unregulated trade and rapid international spread. Biodiversity loss compounds zoonotic risk; conservation policy protects ecosystem health and human health.

articleSummary: African swine fever is not transmissible to humans, but it causes near 100% mortality in pigs. In Vietnam, about 5 tons of infected pigs were culled in Can Tho City after outbreaks across four communes and wards. Earlier, Tay Ninh reported 16 outbreaks since the year began, and Cao Bang saw outbreaks in multiple communes with hundreds of pigs culled. Visual signs in infected meat include hemorrhages on the skin and ears turning purple, abnormal meat colors (brown, dark red, gray), softness, and mucus or loss of elasticity; slaughtered organs often hemorrhage. Authorities urge strict control of transport and sale; consumers should buy from reputable sources, ensure veterinary quarantine, cook thoroughly, separate raw and cooked, and avoid suspicious meat.

articleSummary: Post-weaning diarrheal syndrome in pigs is addressed with a One Health approach to reduce antibiotic reliance. This integrated approach aims for sustainable, antibiotic-reduced pig health.

articleHeadline: Structure of Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus RNA polymerase - Nature Microbiology
articleSummary: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) RNA polymerase L protein was expressed in insect cells, purified, and shown to have RdRp activity in a primer-extension assay using a 24-nt vRNA template and a 6-nt FAM-labeled primer; activity is Mn2+-dependent, with detectable synthesis at 2 mM MnCl2 and reduced at Mg2+ or lower Mn. Cryo-EM yielded apo and RNA-bound structures at 2.62 Å and 2.53 Å, revealing the core L (residues 926-3227) with flexible N- and C-termini. Conserved RdRp motifs A–E and a priming loop were identified; cap-snatching is suggested but a functional CBD remains unclear. The findings clarify polymerase architecture and replication/transcription mechanisms in CCHFV.

articleSummary: Researchers at the Institute of Physics of São Carlos (IFSC/USP) in São Carlos, Brazil, tested whether high-frequency ultrasound—within medical imaging ranges—could damage respiratory viruses. In experiments using frequencies from 3 to 20 MHz, viruses tested included SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A (H1N1). After exposure, viruses appeared smaller, fragmented, and structurally compromised, and their infectivity in cell culture was markedly reduced; SARS-CoV-2 showed substantial loss of ability to infect cells, with replication nearly halted in some cases. The proposed mechanism is resonance—vibrations directly perturb virus particles—rather than heating or cavitation typical of some industrial ultrasound. The work, conducted with collaborators from UNESP (Presidente Prudente) and reported in Scientific Reports, suggests potential applicability to other spherical viruses such as H5N1, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV-1/2), varicella-zoster virus (VZV), and arboviruses like dengue, chikungunya, and Zika, though further research is needed.

articleSummary: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) advances in Asia, with Nepal reporting 23 affected poultry farms last week and culling over 113,000 birds; total birds affected direct/indirectly exceed 142,000 per OIE. Outbreaks are concentrated in Sunsari, Morang, Jhapa, and Chitwan, mainly in Koshi Province near the India border. Measures include destruction of eggs, feed, and contaminated materials, with producer compensation up to 75%. Likely origin from wild birds; risk amplified by migratory proximity, weak biosafety, and movement of people, vehicles, and inputs. In South Korea, 21 new farm outbreaks involve more than 2.5 million birds (Feb–Mar); since Sep 2025, over 6 million birds affected across 56 production units, with H5N1 and H5N9 detected (over 1 million birds since December). The Philippines remain active, concentrated on Luzon; Israel detects cases in wild birds; Cambodia reports domestic and human cases. China and Taiwan report human infections with multiple strains, including first local H7N7; sustained human transmission risk remains low. Enhanced biosafety and surveillance are essential to safeguard global poultry production and markets.
notes: ネパール、韓国、カンボジア、イスラエル、台湾も発生地域に含まれるが、対象国リストにないため除外。記事はアジア全域での高病原性鳥インフルエンザの同時多発的な大規模発生を報告。ネパールで142,000羽以上、韓国で600万羽以上が感染・処分。中国と台湾ではヒト感染事例（H7N7含む）報告。国際的なサプライチェーン・家禽生産への直接的な脅威が明確。

articleHeadline: Horrorkullancs: halálos betegségeket terjeszthet, és Magyarországon is megjelent
articleSummary: Hungary is facing an invasion by the Hyalomma tick, spread by migratory birds and able to survive in the changing climate. The tick can carry Lyme disease, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF) with about a 30% fatality rate, and tick-borne encephalitis. In Hungary, only a few dozen Hyalomma ticks have been found so far, mostly on larger animals, and laboratory tests have not detected infection in them. Nevertheless, there is a risk that CCHF could be imported into the country via animals or birds. Public health authorities (HUN-REN Ökológiai Kutatóközpont) are monitoring its spread and urge residents to report sightings. Prevention is key: avoid unmanaged, bushy areas; wear closed shoes and clothing; and remove a tick promptly after a bite, since transmission is not strictly limited to long attachments.
notes: 記事の主要な主題はハンガリーにおけるヒアロンママダニの出現であるが、ハンガリーは対象国リストに含まれていない。DRCが記事サマリーに登場するのはマダニの学名（Hyalomma congoi）にコンゴが含まれる可能性があるためと推測されるが、記事本文ではDRCでの具体的な発生状況は述べられていない。ただし、IHR基準2つ以上該当しており、WPRO基準で5つ全て該当するため、シグナル検出基準を満たしているが、対象国での確実な発生状況が不明確であることから、まずはWATCHとして続報の収集を推奨する。

articleSummary: Measles imported to Hong Kong from Indonesia in a 39-year-old woman who developed fever and cough on 5 April, with a rash on 7 April. She sought care at Eastern District Hospital and was hospitalized on 9 April; she has recovered and been discharged. The Center for Health Protection says she was unvaccinated and travelled to Indonesia during the incubation period, where measles is ongoing. During the infectious period (3–11 April), she visited Eastern District Hospital (7–9 April) and a clinic, and daily visited Tung Wah Eastern Hospital (3–5 April) to see a patient. By 16 April 2026, 187 close contacts have been identified; none symptomatic so far, and medical monitoring continues. Immunity: those born before 1967 may have natural immunity; those born 1967 or later without two MMR doses should consult a GP. Travellers from high-incidence areas with fever and rash should seek care promptly and avoid contact with unimmunized individuals.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Rospotrebnadzor assessed the risk of the plague spreading from the United States to Russia.
articleHeadline: В Роспотребнадзоре оценили риск распространения чумы из США в России
articleSummary: Rospotrebnadzor is closely monitoring a new plague case in the United States (Arizona this year) but says there is no risk of spread to Russia. The Russian epidemiological situation remains stable due to preventive and monitoring measures. Russia has 11 natural plague foci, seven transboundary along borders with Kazakhstan, Mongolia, China, Azerbaijan, and Georgia. Ongoing epizootic monitoring and joint expeditions occur with Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Kyrgyzstan, and since 2025 Madagascar. Over the past five years, 29 joint outbreak-response exercises engaged over 1,500 specialists. Each year, several thousand doses of Russian anti-plague vaccine are supplied to CIS countries. The plague is caused by Yersinia pestis, circulating among small mammals and fleas; human infection can occur via contact with infected tissues, airborne transmission in pneumonic form, or flea bites. Antibiotics treat the disease.
notes: 記事はロシア当局による危機管理コミュニケーション（リスク評価と予防措置の強調）であり、中国はカザフスタン・モンゴルとの国境でペスト自然病巣を共有する対象国として言及されている。アメリカでの症例と対象国での現在の発生状況の関連性は記事内で示唆されていない。継続的な監視が必要。

articleHeadline: El lado desconocido del mosquito: así detectan y rodean a humanos para contagiar enfermedades... y así podrían salvar vidas
articleSummary: Researchers in China propose using the mosquito Aedes aegypti as a vaccine delivery vector to immunize bats, a key reservoir for Nipah virus and rabies, with the goal of reducing spillover to humans. In a Science Advances study from Kunming Medical University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, mosquitoes fed on blood containing an rVSV-based vaccine encoding Nipah and rabies antigens, after which the virus replicates in the mosquito and is transmitted via saliva during feeding. Vaccinated bites conferred protection in rodent and bat models, and simulations of natural encounters induced strong immune responses in bats, supporting feasibility beyond the lab. An oral approach—saltwater stations—also elicited antibodies. Separately, MIT and Georgia Tech modeled 3D mosquito flight, showing three host-seeking patterns driven by visual silhouettes and carbon dioxide, advancing vector-control insights. Published 2026-04-16.
notes: 記事サマリーはニパ・ウイルスと狂犬病の人獣共通感染症制御に関する中国の研究成果（昆明医科大学・中国科学院）を主題としている。Bluedot APIが付与した「Georgia」および「United States」は研究機関（MIT、Georgia Tech）の所在地であり、実際の感染症イベント発生地ではないため除外した。Malaysia も発生地としての記載がサマリーに明示されていないため除外。発生地域のうち、実際のイベント（ワクチン研究・試験）が行われているのは中国（Yunnan Sheng/Kunming）のみ。

articleHeadline: Kasus Campak Naik Tipis Seusai Lebaran, DIY Tetap Aman
articleSummary: Measles cases in the Yogyakarta Special Region (DIY), Indonesia, rose modestly after Eid al-Fitr 2026 but remain under control, with 112 cases reported as of 6 April 2026, up from 94 before Lebaran. Most infections are mild; there have been no deaths. High vaccination coverage is cited as the key factor limiting spread, with first-dose measles-rubella (MR) vaccination above 98% and second-dose at 96%. Surveillance through SKDR indicates sustained disease monitoring. The elevated mobility during holidays and a simultaneous measles outbreak in Central Java raise importation risk, prompting continued vigilance. Authorities reinforce immunization, especially for children aged 9–59 months, and encourage catch-up MR vaccination for those not fully vaccinated: complete two MR doses if never received, or begin and finish the first and second doses as needed.

articleHeadline: Estado de SP registra primeiros casos de febre amarela do ano e vacinação é intensificada na região do Vale do Paraíba
articleSummary: Three confirmed yellow fever cases were reported by São Paulo’s CVE-SP in the Vale do Paraíba region on 16 April 2026: in Cruzeiro, a 23-year-old woman and a 52-year-old man recovered; in Cunha, a 38-year-old man died. None had prior vaccination. Yellow fever vaccination is free at UBS health units and remains the main preventive tool; the state immunization program has recommended vaccination statewide since 2019. Travelers to risk areas should be vaccinated at least 10 days before travel. Authorities urge checking vaccination status before visiting forested, rural, or ecotourism zones, and to report suspected human cases and epizooties in non-human primates promptly to guide response. Cases and deaths are tracked on the SES-SP dashboard. Vaccination schedule: routine doses at 9 months with a second at 4 years, and a single dose for those aged 5+ without vaccination or proof.

articleSummary: 43-year-old man in Shenzhen, Guangdong, diagnosed with Q fever (Coxiella burnetii) after a week of fever unresponsive to antibiotics. Blood broad-range metagenomic sequencing identified Coxiella burnetii; imaging showed no obvious focal infection in lungs, abdomen, or brain; inflammatory markers elevated. Q fever, a rare zoonosis, primarily transmits from livestock (cattle, sheep) and occasionally cats and dogs; human-to-human transmission is rare; ticks can also transmit. Infection occurs mainly via inhalation of aerosols containing pathogen from animal waste, secretions, or placentas. Symptoms include fever, severe headache, sore throat, cough, chest pain, and commonly liver involvement with abnormal liver function and jaundice; myocarditis, nephritis, myelitis, encephalitis may occur; severe cases can be fatal. A prior Jiangsu, China case last year reported extensive bilateral lung lesions. Pets should undergo regular health checks to reduce risk of transmission.
notes: 記事サマリーより、深圳（広東省）と江蘇省の複数の確定例が報告されている。Q熱は稀な人畜共通感染症であり、抗生物質耐性の可能性と重症合併症リスク（肺炎、脳炎、心筋炎など）が懸念される。血清メタゲノミクスによる診断確定は信頼性が高い。動物との接触歴の確認と接触者調査が重要。

articleHeadline: Sốt xuất huyết Dengue tại miền Trung - Tây Nguyên: Không chỉ mùa mưa, không chừa độ tuổi
articleSummary: Dengue fever is now year-round in Central Vietnam's Central Highlands, with transmission beyond the rainy season and a shortened outbreak cycle (3–4 years). In Da Nang, 2025 saw 4,176 dengue cases and 1 death, with transmission across all communes and year-long activity; by Q1 2026 cases rose 47% year-on-year to 691. Across the Central–Highlands, Dak Lak reported over 560 cases in all 24 districts (+26%), Gia Lai 794, and Quang Ngai 288 (+35%). Adults over 15 accounted for more than 63% of Da Nang cases. Severe dengue requiring intensive care, repeated dialysis or plasma exchange was observed, including neonates and young children with neurological complications; multi-organ involvement is possible. Warning signs between days 3–7 include persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding, and altered consciousness. Prevention emphasizes eliminating standing water, larval control, and bed nets; note that there are four dengue serotypes, enabling up to four infections, with heterotypic infections riskier.
notes: 記事サマリーが詳細にダナン市と中央高地地域の症例増加、重症度、全年齢層への影響、および従来の季節パターンからの逸脱を明確に述べている。神経学的合併症や多臓器関与の可能性があり、重症度と流行性の両面で懸念がある。IHR基準を2項目以上満たし、WPRO基準を4項目すべて満たすためPICKUPと判定。

articleSummary: Vietnam reports 24 meningococcal disease cases this year, with 46% in children under 15. Vietnam currently circulates five serogroups: A, B, C, Y, W. Vaccines covering A/C/Y/W (MenQuadfi, Nimenrix, Menactra) and group B (Bexsero), plus BC vaccines, offer broad protection; full immunization is essential, especially for children, students, and teens in crowded settings. Rising other infections in schools heighten outbreak risk.

Absolute risk is about 36 cases of GBS per 1,000,000 dengue infections. From 2023–2024, >5,000 hospitalizations for GBS were identified, with 89 occurring soon after dengue. Public health implications include adding post-dengue GBS to surveillance, ensuring ICU beds and ventilatory support during dengue outbreaks, and active GBS surveillance in the weeks after dengue peaks. Early recognition enables prompt treatment with immunoglobulin or plasmapheresis. There is no antiviral dengue treatment; prevention through vector control and vaccination remains key. Brazil logged >6 million probable dengue cases in 2024, underscoring arbovirus-related neurological risks similar to Zika.
notes: 記事はブラジル（バイア州）で2026年4月16日にFiocruz研究機関が発表した研究に基づく。デング感染後のGBS発症リスクが従来より高いこと（17～30倍）の公式報告であり、監視体制の強化や医療資源の充実が必要とされている。2024年の大規模デング流行（600万件以上）の文脈での重要な神経学的合併症の証拠。

articleHeadline: Characteristics and immune dynamics of peripheral blood immune cells and cytokines in individuals with chronic hepatitis B virus infection - Scientific Reports
articleSummary: In chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, peripheral blood immune profiling reveals stage-dependent immune shifts. Compared with healthy controls, initial CHB shows higher total B cells and lower CD4+ T cells; CXCL10 is markedly elevated and positively correlates with B cell frequency. CHB patients with HBsAg <1500 ng/mL exhibit higher CXCL10 than those with ≥1500 ng/mL. In late-stage HBV infection (HBV-LC/HBV-HCC), NK cell frequency declines while T-cell frequency increases relative to CHB and controls. Late-stage patients also show higher circulating levels of IFN-γ, IL-6, TNF-α, CCL2, and TNFRI, indicating heightened proinflammatory signaling. Overall, CXCL10, NK cells, and multiple cytokines track disease stage and HBsAg levels, suggesting potential biomarkers for monitoring CHB progression and informing immune-based therapies. articleSummary: Cryo-EM structures of Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) RNA-dependent RNA polymerase L protein reveal two functional states, apo at 2.62 Å and RNA-bound at 2.53 Å, the first atomic-level characterization of a nairovirus RdRp. RNA engagement induces conformational changes that prime catalysis by stabilizing key motifs. Active-site residues enable rational drug design for inhibitors targeting the active site or allosteric pockets, aiming to block replication and ameliorate disease outcomes. This work provides a foundation for therapeutic strategies against CCHFV, a global hemorrhagic fever pathogen with high fatality rates.

Symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, and fatigue; pneumonia is a major complication in infants and the elderly. Vaccination is updated annually to match circulating strains.

articleHeadline: Quase dois meses depois, governo gaúcho dá por encerrado o foco de gripe aviária na Reserva Ecológica do Taim - Jornal O Sul
articleSummary: Avian influenza focus at the Taim Ecological Reserve in Santa Vitória do Palmar, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, was declared closed on 16 April 2026 after 28 days with no new wild bird deaths. The outbreak began in late February when dead wild birds, including coscoroba swans, were found at Lagoa da Mangueira. In response, Seapi mobilized teams using boats and drones; 95 surveillance actions within 10 km around the focus on subsistence poultry holdings, and 22 inspections of regional poultry farms to verify biosafety. Avian influenza is a highly contagious viral disease affecting birds and, less commonly, mammals and humans. Public health guidance urges avoiding contact with injured or dead animals and reporting suspicions (respiratory or neurological signs and sudden mortality) to Seapi via WhatsApp at (51) 98445-2033. Monitoring continues with ICMBio; the reserve reopens. Laboratory confirmation follows WHO NIC criteria; Brazil's NICs: Fiocruz (RJ), IAL (SP), IEC (PA).

articleHeadline: Geriatric Tuberculosis: Five-Year Study Insights India
articleSummary: Five-year retrospective study at a tertiary care hospital in India on tuberculosis in patients aged 60+. Elderly TB is linked to immunosenescence and comorbidities; clinical presentation often diverges from younger patients, causing diagnostic delays. Pulmonary TB predominates, with extrapulmonary manifestations. The elderly show higher infection rates and more severe progression due to reduced lung function and reactivation of latent infections. Socioeconomic and environmental factors—reduced mobility, limited healthcare access, and low SES—worsen outcomes. Drug resistance is more common, complicating regimens and suggesting longer, individualized therapy. Smear microscopy has limited sensitivity in the elderly; authors advocate molecular diagnostics (NAAT) for early detection. Co-morbidities like diabetes, COPD, and malnutrition worsen prognosis and resource use. Gender differences: men more pulmonary; women more extrapulmonary. Psychosocial factors—stigma, isolation, and depression—affect adherence. BCG limitations in elderly; need for age-tailored vaccines. Calls for trained geriatric TB care, better surveillance, and funding for advanced diagnostics and therapeutics.
notes: 本記事は学術的な研究論文・解説であり、感染症の新規発生・クラスター・流行の報告ではない。高齢者結核の臨床的特徴と診断・治療上の課題についての知見を述べているが、シグナル検知対象外として扱う。

articleSummary: Measles in Hong Kong: A 39-year-old unvaccinated woman was laboratory-confirmed with measles after traveling to Indonesia during the incubation period. Symptoms started 5 April with fever, productive cough and sore throat; rash appeared 7 April. She sought care at Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital and was admitted to Eastern District Hospital on 9 April; she recovered and was discharged. The infection is imported; infectious period 3–11 April. She also visited Tung Wah Eastern Hospital from 3–5 April. CHP identified 187 close contacts as of 16 April: one household contact, two companions to medical visits, and others in the same facilities; no contacts have developed measles symptoms yet. The patient had not been vaccinated. CHP continues investigation and monitoring; urges vaccination for all, including domestic workers and airport staff. Outbreaks persist in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, with Indonesia, the Philippines and Cambodia affected, underscoring the need for high vaccination coverage and herd immunity.

articleSummary: Bird Flu (H5N1 avian influenza) detected at a government-run poultry farm in Hesaraghatta, Bengaluru. Central directives guided testing, which confirmed infection in chickens; the farm is closed and precautionary measures tightened as poultry from the area feeds other parts of the state. State veterinary authorities quarantined farm workers and ordered surveillance of nearby poultry sheds, with gram panchayat notices and heightened checks at poultry procurement centers and shops. Experts warn the virus spreads rapidly in higher temperatures and can affect humans and other animals. Public health guidance urges strict hygiene, avoiding contact with infected birds, and ensuring food safety by thoroughly cooking poultry and eggs and avoiding raw eggs or undercooked meat. The World Health Organization has cautioned about potential human transmission.

articleSummary: Measles outbreak alert at RSUD Gunung Jati Cirebon, Indonesia, with about 50 patients hospitalized over January–March and two deaths from pulmonary complications among the unvaccinated. The measles virus (rubeola, Paramyxovirus) spreads via droplets and presents with high fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and widespread red rash. RSUD Gunung Jati serves as a referral center for measles cases from multiple facilities, receiving patients through Emergency Department (IGD) and outpatient care. From January to mid-April 2026, IGD admissions were 26 (Jan), 19 (Feb), and 5 (Mar), totaling roughly 50 by March 31. Outpatient referrals were fewer: 3 (Jan), 0 (Feb), 2 (Mar), 1 (by Apr 16), for a total of about 6. The hospital cautions that community cases are likely higher than hospital admissions, indicating gaps in surveillance and immunization coverage.

articleHeadlineTranslated: A new deadly virus has begun to spread in Russia.
articleHeadline: Новый смертоносный вирус начал распространяться в России
articleSummary: As of 17 April 2026, three monkeypox cases have been reported in Russia, per TASS, epidemiologist Gennady Onishchenko. Monkeypox is a viral disease transmitted from animals to humans and between people. Early symptoms include fatigue, high fever, headache, back and muscle pain; lymphadenopathy differentiates it from varicella and measles. Within 1–3 days after fever, a rash develops from red spots to pustules; severe cases can involve pneumonia, sepsis, encephalitis, or corneal damage, with possible death. On April 13, one case was diagnosed in Moscow region; in March two residents of Saint Petersburg; in February two residents of Neva region who had returned from Thailand. Russia has a monkeypox drug, NIOH-14, developed by Vector, approved for adults 18+, with contraindications pregnancy, breastfeeding, lactose intolerance, or component sensitivity. First monkeypox case was Sept 1, 1970 in DRC. Pandemic risk is linked to four pathogens—avian influenza, Oropush fever, rubella, and monkeypox—and border controls.
